name: Molof
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Sanjoko, Yohanis. 2010. Pola suku kata bahasa Molof [Syllable patterns of the Molof language]. Kibas Cenderawasih 6(1): 67-78. Jayapura: Balai Bahasa Provinsi Papua. DOI 10.26499/kc.v6i1.58
sources.note: Nothing. The only first-hand phonological publication on Molof: syllable templates V, VK, KV, KVK and their combinations in 1-4 syllable words, phoneme distribution within syllables, phonetic transcriptions without stress marks; the word 'tekanan' (stress) never occurs. States (p.68) that the structure of Molof 'belum pernah didokumentasikan dan diteliti' (has never been documented or studied).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-221 [msl] (Randy Lebold, SIL): add name 'Poule'.
sources.note: Nothing; administrative. Names the source 'Survey report on the Poule (Molof) Language. Draft survey report' from SIL's March 2005 rapid-appraisal survey (= Rumaropen 2005).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry AV no. 117 Molof (p. 45): village Molof, +/-200 speakers, sources Galis 1955, 1956b, Voorhoeve 1971; 40-item wordlist in appendix; no structural notes.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. TransNewGuinea.org: Molof (lexicon from Voorhoeve 1971, 1975).
sources.note: Nothing; 118 lexical items, unmarked for stress; sources listed are only Voorhoeve 1971 and 1975.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In Dutton et al. (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.7 'Unclassified languages' (pp. 77-78): Molof 200 speakers; 'The only data available is the word lists collected by Galis (1956b)'; cognate percentages only, no phonology for Molof.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Molof', Provinsi Papua (idb=519).
sources.note: Nothing; villages (Warley, Molof, Purwasi, Tawasi, Tiarsi) and dialectometric distance (98-100% different from Tofanma, Yafi, Dubu) only.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: 'Poule (Molof)' page under Pauwasi River.
sources.note: Nothing; stub page: 'The inclusion of Poule in the Pauwasi River family is highly tentative.'

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. n.d. Molof phonology notes (unpublished manuscript; source of the consonant/vowel inventory in Foley 2018 Tables 27-28).

sources.note: The only phonological description of Molof by a phonologist; if any statement on Molof stress exists it is here. Obtainable only from the author (or via Foley).

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of Northwest New Guinea. In B. Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 433-568. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Sec. 4.6 'The isolate Molof (Poule)' (c. pp. 492-495).

sources.note: Full text of sec. 4.6 would confirm whether Foley relays anything from Donohue's MS beyond the phoneme tables (e.g. a remark on stress or tone); only snippets were readable.

sources.citation: Rumaropen, Benny. 2005. Laporan sosiolinguistik bahasa Poulle di Kampung Molof dan Waley, Kabupaten Keerom, Papua, Indonesia. 28 pp. SIL Indonesia, Jayapura (unpublished draft survey report; cited in ISO 639-3 CR 2007-221 and Foley 2018).
